testcase.name: S052: same key + same body replays the stored 201 and body without a second row; same key + different body is CONFLICT with no effect
a rejected command rolls its reservation back: no journal row survives, and the key is free for the next attempt
a concurrent duplicate waits on the identity index until the first transaction commits, then REPLAYs; after a rollback it proceeds as first
a RESERVED or UNCERTAIN entry that outlives its transaction replays as PENDING; commit() completes only a RESERVED entry; a committed entry is final
CreateAgency reservations (no tenant) are visible to the identity that reserved them and to no other identity
S089 (structural): the request journal refuses a short hash, a zero ceiling and an absent grant; fence-scoped updates; response before consume; terminal states final

S089 failed upstream through the adapter: a dispatch intent naming an upstream that failed, was cancelled, is uncertain, is not yet consumed, is unknown or belongs to another agency is refused UPSTREAM_UNRESOLVED and materializes nothing; naming consumed upstreams it is RESERVED; an upstream that fails or is consumed concurrently is ordered before the reservation
outbox ordering by aggregate version: events of one aggregate are appended in version order, their outbox rows follow the same sequence, and a duplicate version or a label payload is refused

S090 through the adapter: claim, HELD, checkpoint under the fence, refused resumes (no or another checkpoint, reset deadline, another subject, another cost authority), a valid takeover that keeps subject, clock, cost and checkpoint identity, advances the fence and fences the old owner out
a refused claim does not abort the unit of work: a sweeper claims several leases in one transaction and answers each refusal on its own
request handlers have no access to leases (kauro_app has no policy and no grant); a zero ttl is refused before the database
S089/S090-style cross-agency reads: agency B's context finds none of A's rows by id, by lock, by list or by hash; the oracle sees both
cross-agency writes: a row whose agency_id is not the bound context fails WITH CHECK before any FK; the compare-and-swap of a foreign row is NOT_FOUND

composite foreign keys (R2-058/R2-059 as designed): a project of B referencing A's client, and a client of B referencing A's authority, are refused as INVALID_REQUEST / UNKNOWN_REFERENCE even inside B's valid context
a valid project pair commits together: project + DRAFT revision, current_revision bound by the deferred key, events for both versions
an IDENTITY context sees its own identity facts, memberships and agencies and nothing else; a member of another agency has no live membership here
the control plane (kauro_control) has no policy on tenant aggregates: a SYSTEM context reads no agency, membership or client and cannot write one
keyset pagination inside the tenant: a total ordering by (createdAt, clientId) with a cursor that cannot cross the agency
the harness applied every migration from an empty cluster and the pools run as unprivileged members of one runtime group
a pool refuses a superuser login and the owner login before any statement runs (08: privileged roles never serve requests)
a context runs only on the pool of its role: SYSTEM is refused on the request pool, TENANT and IDENTITY on the control pool
commit persists everything; a thrown DomainFailure rolls everything back and is rethrown as the business outcome
an unexpected exception becomes INTERNAL_ERROR carrying only the correlation id; the cause stays server-side
a connection returned to the pool carries no context after commit, rollback and exception (08: cleared on pool return)
the deferred event-per-version rule fires at COMMIT: an aggregate written without its event is refused as INTEGRITY_FAILURE / EVENT_MISSING and nothing persists
adoptTenant: only an IDENTITY context, only once, only with an id minted in this unit of work; resolveMembership: TENANT only, once
CreateAgency through the adapters (CMD001-OK shape): one DRAFT agency, one ACTIVE OWNER membership, two events, one outbox row, journal COMMITTED, all in one transaction
SERIALIZABLE with bounded retries: a serialization failure re-runs the work in a fresh transaction and both units of work commit exactly once
statement_timeout is transaction-local: a lock wait past the ceiling fails that unit of work as CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE, the holder proceeds, and the connection returns without the setting
compare-and-swap writes: a stale expected version applies nothing and returns the current safe version and state; an invisible row is NOT_FOUND
the last active owner cannot be removed through the membership repository: PRECONDITION_FAILED / LAST_OWNER_PROTECTED (R2-043 at the adapter boundary)
an aggregate change without a version bump, a version skip, or a version bump without its event cannot commit
unlisted transitions and immutable columns are refused; archiving (CMD010) is the listed edge and deletes nothing

S051: two revisions racing on one plan version through the plan adapter — one compare-and-swap applies, the loser waits on the row lock and reads STALE with the current version; a second successor of the same predecessor is refused by plans_supersedes_once
an approval binds exact plan/source/target/receipt hashes; a foreign or stale hash cannot be recorded; one live approval per plan
outbox records commit with their event under the tenant policy and can only name events of the bound tenant

N20: the dispatcher claims due records of its consumer with their event, delivers under the attempt it claimed, retries, dead-letters, and a claim that expired and was taken again settles nothing (FENCED)
N20: two dispatchers claiming at once take disjoint records (SKIP LOCKED), and the request handlers can neither claim nor settle a record
N20: the consumer claims recorded provider events once (PROCESSING), settles them once, reclaims a stale claim, and deduplication is by provider, environment and event id
R3: an event names an aggregate of its own agency — agency A's runtime role can neither occupy B's next client version nor tell B's ids from unknown ones, and B's own event still commits
R4: the control plane reads the command journal's safe technical metadata across tenants, never the journaled response, the key, the digest or the actor
R5/R13: an approval binds its actor, the actor's own membership in this agency and a step-up proof of that same actor

R5 (acting session): an approval and its withdrawal are acts of the session's own identity — nobody records an approval in the approver's name, even with the approver's membership and fresh proof, nor a withdrawal under another member's membership; the approver's own session and the owner's own membership can
R11: a plan names only its own approval — pointing plan Y at plan X's approval is refused at COMMIT and Y stays VALIDATED
R6: the request handlers can neither read nor rewrite any inbox row; the ingress records a provider event once, as a receipt; the control plane consumes it

N2: an agency's request handler can no longer pre-insert a provider event id to suppress the genuine delivery — only the ingress records provider events, and a same-id delivery with another body is recorded as a conflict that blocks applying the event
R10: active_owner_count is written only by the membership trigger — the runtime role can neither raise it by hand nor forge it at birth, so the last real owner stays protected
R14: step-up proofs are written only by the step-up verifier — the request handlers cannot mint one, not even their own; the verifier writes only for the identity it binds and reads nothing
R14/R30: a verifier or validator login is its own runtime group — it runs no request-handler unit of work, and a login in two groups is refused by the verified pool
R20: every aggregate is born in its machine's initial state — a row inserted in a later state is refused as the runtime role that would write it (KA008)

R20: the founding owner of CreateAgency is the one membership born ACTIVE — a founding ADMIN, a founding owner for somebody else, an owner written by another session and a second owner are all refused
R30: validation receipts are written only by the validator, under the plan's own tenant; a plan binds only a VALID receipt of its own body and subjects
N19: an invitation is issued by the acting session's own membership with the authority to grant its role, for an INVITED membership of exactly that role, one open at a time

N19: only the invited identity consumes its invitation, once, before its deadline; the stored token is only a digest; a closed invitation never reopens; the invitee finds it by token without a tenant context
N19: team authority revokes an open invitation (an ADMIN never one of an OWNER role); concurrent consumptions produce one acceptance

S052: through the command journal adapter the same digest replays the stored response and a different digest under the same key is CONFLICT with no second row; the identity index makes the key unique, a committed entry is final, the same key in another agency is another identity
a concurrent duplicate blocks on the identity until the first transaction commits, then sees the committed entry; after a rollback it proceeds as first
CreateAgency reservations (no tenant) are visible to the identity that reserved them and to no other identity

S089: a request journal entry cannot be materialized with a short SHA, without a positive reservation, without a grant or with an upstream that is not resolved (failed, cancelled, uncertain, unconsumed, unknown, of another scope, repeated or itself); the valid controls commit
S090: a lease preserves subject, deadline, cost and checkpoint identity across a takeover; a resume without the checkpoint, with a reset deadline, another subject or another cost authority is refused
two owners removing each other: one transition commits, the other is refused — its actor's authority ended with the first commit (KA010); one owner remains

two owners leaving at once (each revoking their own ownership while reading two active owners): one commits, the other waits on the agency row lock and is refused with LAST_OWNER (KA001); one owner remains
the sole owner cannot revoke themselves; a non-owner can be revoked; closure authority permits the removal
a suspension of the last owner is refused the same way (the invariant covers every listed edge)
R33: two runners started at once on a fresh database serialize on the runner lock — both succeed, one applies every migration, the other re-reads the ledger under the lock and skips them
R37: the migrator is bounded — a host that accepts and never answers refuses within the connect timeout, and a lock held on the ledger refuses within the lock timeout instead of hanging the start
every migration applied once, in order, with its checksum recorded; a second run applies nothing
a migration file edited after being applied is refused as drift
runtime roles are neither owners nor superusers and have no BYPASSRLS; the owner never serves requests
state and enum CHECK constraints carry exactly the registry vocabularies
the listed-transition seed equals the registry machines for every machine the schema guards
R20: the initial-state seed equals the registry machines (and the platform machines of D-AGG-1/D-AGG-2); every table that guards its listed edges also guards its birth state
registered event types in the database are exactly the domain EVENT_TYPES
R46: the production entry point exports no test helper; the test-only subpath @kauro/persistence/testing does
R47: every declared workspace dependency is imported, and the pg types the public declarations name are a pinned runtime dependency
R38: an idle connection the server terminates reaches the pool's error sink as pool name, class and SQLSTATE — never the message or a connection parameter
R38: without a configured sink the classification is written to stderr, one line, and nothing is swallowed

R38: a connection the server terminates while a unit of work holds it fails that unit of work and reaches the sink as an in-use connection error — no error event is left unhandled, and the pool then serves a fresh connection

N1: the request-handler role holds no privilege on an identity's security status — it cannot lift a DISABLED row, its own included, nor be born anything but ACTIVE; its sync keeps only the verification facts current
N5: ending an approval moves its plan out of APPROVED in the same transaction — a withdrawal written alone, leaving the plan APPROVED under no live authority, is refused at COMMIT (KA020)
N6: a label refuses exactly the Unicode control characters (C0, DEL and C1) by code point, whatever the cluster's locale; a refusal that reaches the database names its field

N9: a plan's source and target are a sealed revision and a target contract of its own project — naming another project's is refused at insert, whatever the hashes; the plan's subject columns are its body's members

N11: the membership write boundary — a VIEWER's own session cannot promote itself, an ADMIN cannot grant or touch OWNER, only the invited identity accepts and only with a consumed invitation; the OWNER's changes commit
N11: the agency's state and agreements are the OWNER's decisions, and an approval is recorded only by an ACTIVE approving membership of the acting session and withdrawn only by its controller
N11/B06 work: every runtime role's table and column privileges and every row-security policy equal the reviewed matrix

R42: the runtime roles read the ledger (and cannot write it); compared with the shipped migrations it is COMPATIBLE, DRIFTED on a changed checksum, BEHIND on a missing version, and tolerates a newer expand migration

R2: a fact in an agency's stream needs the writer's live membership in that agency — an outsider bound to the agency's context is refused, a member is admitted, a revoked member is refused, and nobody writes as someone else
R2/R26: an identity-owned fact belongs to its writer — it may name the agency the request selected, which need not exist; it is never both in a stream and naming another agency
R26: the anonymous fact — written with no user and no agency bound, by nobody, as a DENY of assurance NONE; refused under any user context, as an ALLOW, or in a stream
R2: an agency's runtime role reads its own stream only — never another agency's facts, never an identity-owned or anonymous fact that names it
R26: the ANONYMOUS context runs on the request-handler pool only, sees no row, and writes nothing but its anonymous fact
the oracle sees both tenants; the runtime role without context sees nothing and cannot write (fail closed)
a tenant context sees exactly its own rows and cannot select, update or insert rows of the other tenant
composite foreign keys refuse a child that references another tenant's parent even inside a valid context
the same connection carries no context after commit, after rollback and after an exception
two pooled connections in different contexts interleave without leaking
a person sees their own memberships and the agencies they belong to without a tenant context, and nothing else
duplicate client labels are two workspaces (labels are presentation, identity is stable)
